solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Maestro after formal wear clothed by worker in Next

indicators.note: to be clothed by something is to be wrapped in it, so the worker goes round the rest

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker

indicators.note: the maestro comes after the formal wear in the build

parts.note: DJ, dinner jacket, is formal evening wear
an ace is a master or expert, a maestro

explanation.surface: A conductor in evening dress is hemmed in by a labourer at the high-street store Next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Next' looks like the fashion retailer but is the definition, meaning neighbouring; DJ is the British short form of dinner jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Something next to another thing is lying beside it, neighbouring it.

clue.text: Where one needs repairman to be responsible?

definitions.meaning: you call a repairman when there is a breakdown, a defect in the works

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the person who needs a repairman is to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Being to blame for a mistake means being culpable; read literally, the phrase places you at a defect needing repair.

clue.text: One blocking post kind about women's hearts

parts.note: a post is a job

indicators.note: the word kind goes about, around, the women

parts.note: a kind is a sort
W abbreviates women
H is the card abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: Someone holding a post is a kind soul who cares about women's feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: A jobsworth is a petty British official who blocks you by sticking rigidly to the rules, 'more than my job's worth'.
explanation.definitionFit: The typical jobsworth obstructs requests with petty rule-keeping, so is someone who blocks.

clue.text: Ordinary addition to a uniform

definitions.meaning: in heraldry an ordinary is one of the simple geometric charges on a shield
a V-shaped stripe sewn on a sleeve to show rank

explanation.surface: Something plain and ordinary is added to a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: The V-shaped band is both a heraldic ordinary and the rank stripe on military sleeves.

clue.text: More than one fool behaves amorously, about to be dumped

indicators.note: dumped means thrown out, so the word for about is removed

parts.note: to canoodle is to kiss and cuddle
CA, circa, means about

explanation.surface: Several fools are carrying on amorously, about to be ditched by their partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is an old informal word for a silly person, so the plural is several fools.

clue.text: Reverend nearly accepts uniform with new cloth

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so the shortened vicar holds the other letters
nearly means the last letter is missing

parts.note: a vicar is a reverend
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A vicar takes on a uniform with fresh cloth for his vestments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cloth' suggests the clergy, but it is the definition of a fabric; 'accepts' puts U and N inside VICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicuña wool, from a wild Andean relative of the llama, is woven into a fine fabric.

clue.text: See old characters are finally used for screen entertainment

parts.note: vide is Latin for see, used in references
ogam is an ancient Celtic alphabet

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Instructions to look at old letters that are at last put to use for a screen show.
explanation.walkthrough: OGAM (also ogham) is the old Irish alphabet of strokes; 'used for' just links wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Played on a monitor or television, this is an electronic pastime, entertainment on a screen.

clue.text: Sausage is cold — and as far as one can see not new

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold

indicators.note: not with new means the abbreviation for new is left out

parts.words: as far as one can see
parts.note: the horizon is the limit of what one can see

explanation.surface: A sausage that is chilled and, so far as anyone can tell, not freshly made.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicy Spanish pork sausage coloured with paprika.

clue.text: Clue sun awkwardly as centre of orbital system

indicators.note: written awkwardly, the letters are put in a clumsy new order

explanation.surface: A clumsy attempt to describe the sun as the centre of its orbiting planets.
explanation.walkthrough: The sun at the centre of the solar system is a red herring; the orbits are those of electrons in an atom.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrons orbit an atom's core, its dense central body of protons and neutrons.

clue.text: Invention concerning food product made from woodchips

parts.note: a fib is a made-up story
re means concerning
board is meals provided, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A newly invented food product made from woodchips, which sounds unappetising.
explanation.definitionFit: Building panels are made by compressing wood fibres or chips with glue.

clue.text: Lose penny from pocket? That hurts

indicators.note: losing the penny means taking its letter out

parts.note: a pouch is a pocket

explanation.surface: Losing a penny from your pocket is painful.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of sudden pain, said when something hurts.

clue.text: Imbue wordplay with a twist, trapping learner rising in standard

indicators.note: trapping means holding something inside
given a twist, the letters are wrenched into a new order

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: An instruction to make wordplay more twisty, with a novice caught up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a twist' rearranges IMBUE WORDPLAY and 'trapping' puts L inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: People moving up the social ladder are climbing in status or standard of living.

clue.text: Never time to back overthrown saint's oppressors

indicators.note: to back means to go backwards, so these words are read in reverse

parts.note: nary means never a, not one

indicators.note: overthrown means turned over, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: ST abbreviates saint

explanation.surface: There is never a moment to support the oppressors of a deposed saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' reverses NARY T to give TYRAN, and 'overthrown' turns ST into TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Despots who rule cruelly are the classic oppressors.

clue.text: One cutting sleep a bit, rising in shape

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, so backwards
one cutting into the other word is placed inside it

parts.note: to doze is to sleep lightly
I is the Roman numeral one
a part is a bit

explanation.surface: Someone getting by on a little sleep and rising in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' puts I into DOZE, then PART is added and 'rising' reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-sided figure with one pair of parallel sides is a geometric shape.

clue.text: See an elk run

parts.note: V is vide, see, in references
the elk is the European name for the moose

explanation.surface: Look at that elk run!
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for clearing off or leaving fast, to scram or run away.

clue.text: Russia's characteristic tearjerker, with accompanying notes

parts.note: cutting an onion makes you weep
do and me are notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Russia's typical tear-jerking drama, with notes from a musical score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tearjerker' suggests a weepy film, but it is an onion; 'with accompanying' only joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulb-shaped cupolas crown Russian Orthodox churches and are a hallmark of Russian architecture.

clue.text: Student's mark cut by incomplete grasp

indicators.note: the mark is cut open by the other part, which goes inside

parts.note: a scar is a mark

indicators.note: incomplete means the final letter is missing

parts.note: a hold is a grasp

explanation.surface: A student's grade is cut because their grasp of the subject is incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person, or one holding a scholarship at a school or college, is a student.

clue.text: Rules about a lot of whip leather

indicators.note: the rules go about, around, the rest

parts.note: a code is a set of rules

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: Rules concerning a large amount of leather for whips.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin of a cow, tanned, is a kind of leather.

clue.text: Working as Roman galley slave?

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Was a Roman galley slave working?
explanation.definitionFit: Galley slaves were chained to the benches as rowers, pulling at the oars.

clue.text: Tired air recycled so as to block tobacco

indicators.note: blocking here means stopping up the middle, so the anagram goes inside

parts.note: weed is slang for tobacco

indicators.note: recycled means processed into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stale, recycled air in a room full of tobacco smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Being made weary means being worn out or tired.

clue.text: Now entering World Trade Organisation. To what end?

indicators.note: entering means going inside the abbreviation

parts.note: WTO is its abbreviation
here can mean now, at this point

explanation.surface: Now joining the World Trade Organisation, but what for?
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned adverb asking for what purpose, to what end.

clue.text: Bearing component unknown in train, initially used too hard

indicators.note: the unknown is put in the word for train

parts.note: to train a gun is to aim it
Z is an algebraic unknown

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: A part of a mechanical bearing, unknown in trains, at first used too hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like a machine part but means a compass direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The angle measured round the horizon from north is one component of a direction or bearing.

clue.text: One covering actor's role in operating theatre

definitions.text: One covering actor's role in operating theatre

parts.words: One covering actor's role in operating theatre
parts.note: in a stage theatre this person clothes actors; in an operating theatre a surgeon's assistant applies bandages to wounds

explanation.surface: An understudy covering an actor's part in a play about a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' seems to mean standing in for, but it is putting clothes or bandages on; the word serves both kinds of theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre wardrobe assistant helps actors into costume, and a hospital assistant applies surgical dressings.

clue.text: What pupils may have to suffer after run

indicators.note: the word for suffer comes after the word for run

parts.note: to run a machine is to work it
to experience something is to undergo or suffer it

explanation.surface: What schoolchildren may have to endure after a cross-country run.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, school pupils spend a week or two in a workplace to learn about jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Placements in a workplace are arranged for school students as part of their education.

clue.text: Cinema turned my life around — coming to no conclusions

indicators.note: turned and around together say the letters are read backwards
with turned, says the remaining letters run in reverse
the two words lose their last letters, never reaching their ends

explanation.surface: Cinema changed my life completely, though nothing was ever resolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to no conclusions' cuts MY and LIFE to M and LIF, and 'turned ... around' reverses MLIF.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinema and film both name the art of motion pictures.

clue.text: Oily, fishy bisque that's got in even pieces of coconuts

indicators.note: something fishy is suspect or off, so the letters are put in a new order
even pieces are the second, fourth and other even-placed letters

explanation.surface: A greasy fish soup with even bits of coconut in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even pieces of' takes OOUS from coconuts, and 'fishy' rearranges these with BISQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unctuous, fawning behaviour is described as oily, excessively eager to please.

clue.text: The contents of Sweeney Todd's last thought in the past

indicators.note: the contents are what lies inside, all but the outer letters
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: What the barber Sweeney Todd's pies contained, thought about long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: To ween is an archaic verb meaning to think or suppose, so its past tense means thought.

clue.text: Like organ's part of chorale arranged by timeless Cage?

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reorders the material, so these letters are rearranged
an age is a span of time, so it is removed from the name

explanation.surface: A chorale for organ arranged by the composer John Cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the instrument, but it is the ear; 'timeless' removes AGE from CAGE, leaving C.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the cochlea, the spiral part of the inner ear, a sense organ.
